issues.description: The problem text instructs students to implement addGuestStudents(String) (textual task description), while the UML diagram in the same problem statement and the reference solution implement addGuestStudents(int). This parameter-type mismatch (String vs int) can confuse students about the correct signature to implement and will cause compile/test failures if they follow the wrong variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: change the textual task description to require addGuestStudents(int) (matching the UML and solution), or alternatively update the UML and solution to use addGuestStudents(String) if that was the intended design. Prefer updating the text to 'addGuestStudents(int)' to match the UML/tests/solution.

issues.description: The problem statement's textual task lists the method as addGuestStudents(String) (suggesting a String parameter), while the UML in the same problem statement and the solution implementation use addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the method signature (parameter type) for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students) can confuse students about the expected parameter type and what they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter type consistent across artifacts. Update the problem statement textual description to specify addGuestStudents(int) (matching the UML and solution), or if a String is intended, update the UML and solution to use addGuestStudents(String). Preferably correct the problem statement to addGuestStudents(int) to avoid student confusion.
